title: Tamoxifen · daily hormone therapy
context_label: ER-positive early or advanced breast cancer
schedule_summary: Take tamoxifen once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The prescriber confirms the duration for the treatment setting.
purpose: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.
indication_text: Adjuvant or advanced oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer in pre- or postmenopausal women, within the exact NCCP eligibility criteria.
administration_text: Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile before treatment. Check clot history, medicines and pregnancy possibility. ECG and electrolytes are added when cardiac / QT risk makes them clinically indicated. Liver tests, INR, ophthalmology and ECG are repeated when clinically indicated. NCCP recommends an annual gynaecological examination; new abnormal vaginal bleeding needs prompt assessment.

agents.name: Tamoxifen
agents.mechanism: Blocks oestrogen signalling at breast-cancer receptors
agents.explanation: Tamoxifen acts at oestrogen receptors. Its effects differ between tissues, which helps explain the distinct blood-clot and womb risks. It is not a cytotoxic chemotherapy infusion.
agents.watch: Report abnormal vaginal bleeding, clot symptoms and visual changes promptly. Discuss hot flushes, sleep and sexual symptoms early.
risks: Hot flushes, sweating and sleep disturbance
Vaginal / sexual symptoms and menstrual changes
Blood clots in the leg or lung; stroke
Liver effects and uncommon serious skin reactions
QT rhythm risk in susceptible patients

urgent_extra: Seek prompt assessment for new one-sided leg swelling, unexpected vaginal bleeding, new visual changes or jaundice. New chest pain, breathlessness or stroke symptoms can signal a serious problem.

sections.title: Make one daily dose easier
sections.text: Link the tablet to a regular daily routine. Ask the pharmacy for help with supply or swallowing difficulties. Do not double a dose to catch up.

sections.title: Surgery, immobility and clot risk
sections.text: Tell the surgical and oncology teams that you take tamoxifen. They decide whether any temporary interruption is needed; there is no automatic fixed interruption for everyone.

sections.title: Bleeding and eye symptoms
sections.text: Do not wait for an annual review to report unusual vaginal bleeding or visual disturbance. An annual gynaecological examination does not mean routine ultrasound or biopsy for an asymptomatic person.

sections.title: Review all medicines
sections.text: Include prescriptions, over-the-counter products and supplements. Some antidepressants can reduce conversion to the active metabolite; a prescriber should review any change.

evidence.title: EBCTCG: adjuvant tamoxifen benefit in ER-positive breast cancer
evidence.population: Individual-patient meta-analysis of 20 randomized trials,21,457 women; ER-positive efficacy population 10,645. About 5 years of tamoxifen versus no adjuvant tamoxifen.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Breast-cancer recurrence and mortality rate ratios by follow-up period.
evidence.interpretation: In ER-positive disease, recurrence rate ratios were 0.53 during years 0–4 and 0.68 during years 5–9; breast-cancer mortality was reduced by about one-third through 15 years.
evidence.limitations: Relative effects are not an individual absolute benefit. Absolute benefit depends on baseline recurrence risk. Historical adjuvant evidence does not quantify benefit in metastatic disease or ER-negative disease.

separate_indication_evidence.title: ATLAS: duration review after five years
separate_indication_evidence.population: 6,846 ER-positive women within 12,894 randomized participants who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen.
separate_indication_evidence.primary_endpoint: Recurrence and breast-cancer mortality after allocation to continue to 10 years or stop at 5 years.
separate_indication_evidence.interpretation: Years 5–14 recurrence:21.4% versus 25.1%; breast-cancer mortality:12.2% versus 15.0%. Extended treatment increased pulmonary embolus risk (RR 1.87) and endometrial-cancer risk (3.1% versus 1.6% during years 5–14).
separate_indication_evidence.limitations: A planned risk–benefit discussion, not automatic ten-year treatment for everyone. Benefit and harm populations differ: cancer efficacy is ER-positive, safety analyses include all receptor groups. Published correction is listed.

teachback: What is your treatment schedule, which checks apply to your setting, and who books and reviews them?
consent_support: History of significant thromboembolic disease is an NCCP exclusion. Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Interactions, including potent CYP2D6 inhibitors, need medication review. Tamoxifen is not contraception. Discuss non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for nine months after stopping, where relevant; absent periods do not prove infertility.

support.title: Symptoms and daily life
support.text: Report abnormal vaginal bleeding, clot symptoms and visual changes promptly. Discuss hot flushes, sleep and sexual symptoms early.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: No routine antiemetic, steroid premedication or G-CSF is required by this endocrine monotherapy. Ask for individual symptom support.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Ask who books each check, when it is due and who reviews it. Tell the team if an expected appointment has not arrived.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.

items.title: Who this card covers
items.text: Adjuvant or advanced oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer in pre- or postmenopausal women, within the exact NCCP eligibility criteria.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 20 mg orally once daily. Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.

items.title: Duration and decision points
items.text: For early breast cancer, discuss the initial endocrine course and a later decision about extending or changing treatment; some patients continue endocrine therapy to 10 years. Advanced treatment continues according to benefit and tolerance. A five-year review is not an automatic instruction to stop.

items.title: Individual safety
items.text: History of significant thromboembolic disease is an NCCP exclusion. Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Interactions, including potent CYP2D6 inhibitors, need medication review.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Baseline, ongoing safety checks and cancer scans have different purposes.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before treatment. Check clot history, medicines and pregnancy possibility. ECG and electrolytes are added when cardiac / QT risk makes them clinically indicated.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Liver tests, INR, ophthalmology and ECG are repeated when clinically indicated. NCCP recommends an annual gynaecological examination; new abnormal vaginal bleeding needs prompt assessment.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: ECG is risk-based. For patients with QT risk, the cited tamoxifen product information recommends baseline ECG / electrolytes and repeat ECG after at least four weeks, with further checks as indicated. Routine echo surveillance is not required for tamoxifen alone.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Assess personal fracture and menopausal risks. Tamoxifen has a different effect on bone from aromatase inhibitors; do not automatically copy an AI bone-density schedule.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After curative treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. The mastectomy side is not routinely mammographed. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended for asymptomatic early-breast surveillance. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy
items.text: In an early-breast pathway, chemotherapy, if indicated, precedes endocrine treatment. Surgery and its pathology guide adjuvant choices. Postoperative radiotherapy is usually delivered after recovery and any adjuvant chemotherapy; aromatase inhibitors may overlap radiotherapy under the agreed plan. Tamoxifen timing around radiotherapy is agreed by the treating teams. None of these additional treatments is automatically required by an endocrine prescription.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: Tamoxifen is not contraception. Discuss non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for nine months after stopping, where relevant; absent periods do not prove infertility.

chapters.title: Evidence for a different decision
chapters.intro: Each study applies to its own population and treatment setting.

items.title: ATLAS: duration review after five years
items.text: 6,846 ER-positive women within 12,894 randomized participants who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen. Years 5–14 recurrence:21.4% versus 25.1%; breast-cancer mortality:12.2% versus 15.0%. Extended treatment increased pulmonary embolus risk (RR 1.87) and endometrial-cancer risk (3.1% versus 1.6% during years 5–14). A planned risk–benefit discussion, not automatic ten-year treatment for everyone. Benefit and harm populations differ: cancer efficacy is ER-positive, safety analyses include all receptor groups. Published correction is listed.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.
